claims.text: Post-process heat treatment of additively manufactured AlCrFeNiSi can overcome residual thermal stresses.
Post-process heat treatment of additively manufactured AlCrFeNiSi can improve degraded mechanical properties.
Post-process heat treatment can reduce the processing complexity associated with conventional additive manufacturing.
The relevant initial material state is AlCrFeNiSi powder feedstock in the as-additively-manufactured condition.
The proposed intervention is post-process heat treatment.
An applicable heat-treatment window is 500–1100 °C with a holding time of 6 hours.
Phase structure and grain size mediate the response to heat treatment.
Heat treatment relieves residual thermal stresses in additively manufactured AlCrFeNiSi.
Heat treatment regulates phase proportions and phase-boundary structures.
Heat treatment enhances mechanical properties through grain refinement and precipitation evolution.
Heat-treated AlCrFeNiSi components will have greater strength and ductility than untreated components made under conventional high-thermal-load additive-manufacturing conditions.
Heat-treated components will have lower processing complexity than untreated components made under conventional high-thermal-load additive-manufacturing conditions.
Heat treatments above 1100 °C may significantly alter the phase structure.
Heat treatments above 1100 °C may degrade mechanical properties.
Optimal heat-treatment temperature and holding time may vary with alloy composition and additive-manufacturing process.
Strength, ductility, hardness, phase structure, grain size, and eutectic morphology can be compared between heat-treated and untreated specimens.

contradictions.description: The initial state is described as powder feedstock in an as-additively-manufactured condition, but an as-manufactured condition applies to a fabricated component rather than feedstock; the intervention and experiment subsequently treat components.
Reduced processing complexity is a predicted outcome and part of the falsification rule, but no processing-complexity metric is included among the measurements.
